subject: Contract execution: Onboarding sprint and MAP for Pinecrest (kickoff & canary windows)
messages:
From: Claire Taylor <claire.taylor@pinecresthealth.com>
To: naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
Cc: mike.huang@pinecresthealth.com
Date: Fri, 3 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Contract signed — next steps for onboarding and MAP

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again — excited to get started. Our procurement team confirmed the signed SOW this morning. We'd like to lock the mutual next steps so we can align internal stakeholders and avoid surprises during the go-live. High level asks from our side:

- A short, deliverable-oriented MAP we can circulate to engineering, security, and Ops.
- A canary plan for the first 2 weeks of traffic with clear rollback gates.
- An evaluation plan (quality & latency thresholds) tied to acceptance criteria.
- Training windows for product and support (2 sessions, week of 4/19).

Can you share a draft MAP and propose dates for the kickoff, canary, and training? We want to avoid peak billing cycles (avoid 4/12–4/16 if possible).

Attachments: none on our side yet.

Best,
Claire
Claire Taylor
VP Product Operations
Pinecrest Health
phone: +1 415-555-0132

---

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Taylor <claire.taylor@pinecresthealth.com>
Cc: Mike Huang <mike.huang@pinecresthealth.com>, jonas.weber@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 3 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Contract signed — next steps for onboarding and MAP

Claire — great news, and congrats to your team. I've attached a first-pass MAP embedded with the post-signature implementation plan and a separate canary checklist. Summary below and asks in bold.

Summary (high level):
- Kickoff: 2027-04-11 10:00 PT (90m) — goals: scope alignment, runbook owners, initial canary windows.
- Canary: 2027-04-19 — 2027-04-30 (staged traffic ramp over 10 business days).
  - Day 1: 1% traffic, smoke tests, acceptance gate A (latency & error rate).
  - Day 3–4: 5% traffic, business-critical prompts evaluation.
  - Day 7: 20% traffic, extended QA and throttling policy test.
  - Roll to 100% after completion of acceptance gate D and a final post-mortem.
- Migration: Rolling routing changes coordinated with your infra team; target low-traffic windows 02:00–05:00 PT.
- Training: two 90-minute live sessions (2027-04-20 and 2027-04-22) + recorded short modules.
- Evaluation plan: We propose pass/fail gates using the MAP evaluation tab with these metrics: median p95 latency < 350ms (tail tokens excluded), error rate < 0.8%, embedding cosine drift < 0.02 against baseline set, and prompt quality score (human-blind eval) >= 88%.

Action items for Pinecrest (bold):
- Please confirm kickoff attendee list and a single technical lead for routing changes (we recommended Mike H.).
- Confirm the training attendee count (we recommend max 20 per live session).
- Provide 3 representative prompt sets and 1 sample dataset for the quality eval by 2027-04-12.

Attachments: 
- MAP_Pinecrest_20270403.xlsx (mutual action plan; tabs: milestones, owners, eval-criteria, training, rollback).
- Canary_Checklist_Pinecrest.pdf (pre-flight and daily checklist).

Notes: We intentionally moved the canary start to 4/19 to avoid the heavy billing window you flagged. If you'd prefer an earlier start we can shift, but will need confirmation from your infra owner.

I'll loop in Jonas (runtime lead) and Marissa (onboarding PM) to propose owners and to draft the runbook entries.

—Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai | +1 650-555-0199

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Claire Taylor <claire.taylor@pinecresthealth.com>, Mike Huang <mike.huang@pinecresthealth.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Apr 2027 14:40:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Contract signed — next steps for onboarding and MAP

Jonas / Marissa — forwarding Claire's note and the MAP (attached). Quick alignment ask: can you each confirm the owner intents below so I can update the MAP owners tab? We want to hand this to Pinecrest at kickoff.

Proposed owners (please confirm or reassign):
- Runtime & canary gating: jonas.weber (Redwood runtime lead) — tasks: define throttling policy, KV cache warmup, automated gates.
- Implementation runbook & day-to-day coordinator: marissa.cole (Redwood onboarding PM) — tasks: daily status, post-canary retro, training logistics.
- Security/questionnaire follow-ups: Naomi Feldman — I'll own SOC/attestation deliverables.

Preliminary draft schedule (from MAP):
- 4/11 Kickoff (90m) — internal dry-run at 9:00 PT same day for Redwood-only 60m.
- 4/12–4/18 Pre-canary: prompt set delivery, environment provisioning, baseline evals.
- 4/19–4/30 Canary ramp.
- 5/03 Post-canary acceptance and handoff.

Risks to call out now:
- Data residency checks from Pinecrest ops may require additional network hops — could add 8–12hrs to provisioning.
- If prompt sets arrive late, the evaluation window compresses and pushes the canary start.

Please reply with confirmed owners and whether we should shorten the internal dry-run.

Thanks,
Naomi

From: Mike Huang <mike.huang@pinecresthealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, jonas.weber@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Contract signed — next steps for onboarding and MAP

Thanks all — this looks good. Quick responses:

- Confirmed: Mike Huang will be Pinecrest's infra lead for routing/migration. I'll be on the kickoff.
- Prompt sets: we'll deliver 3 sets + sample dataset by 2027-04-12 EOD.
- Training: target attendees ~14 (mix of product, support, and 2 SREs). 4/20 and 4/22 sessions work.

Two small asks/edits to the MAP:
1) Can we move the internal Redwood-only dry-run to 8:00 PT on 4/11 (earlier) so our APAC folks can join the later 10:00 session?
2) Add an explicit acceptance gate that requires a pass on a 10-issue human blind eval and signoff from Pinecrest product before moving from 5% -> 20% traffic.

If those are ok we approve the MAP and will circulate to stakeholders this afternoon.

Attachments: none.

Best,
Mike Huang
Lead Infrastructure Engineer
Pinecrest Health
